newsitem.title: USA: Goosebump books too scary for kids?.
newsitem.headline: Goosebump books too scary for kids?.

text.p: Members of the local school board have assigned themselves some homework -- reading R.L. Stine's "Goosebumps" books to see if they're too scary for school libraries.

The Anoka-Hennepin School Board said it will hold public meetings Jan. 14 and 30 to discuss the issue after some of its members on a special committee finish reading at least four of the popular books available in school libraries.
The committee was formed recently in response to a complaint from a parent who said she feared "some children could become paranoid and insecure about daily life" after reading the books.

Cynthia Malone, marketing director of the Scholastic Book Club which sells Stine's and other books through school book clubs, told the St. Paul Pioneer-Press in a story published Friday that to her knowledge the Goosebump books have not been banned from any schools.
The evening TV news is probably more frightening, she told the newspaper.
